note: Plan row R13. The hypotheses, rules, parameters, markets, timeframes, gates and verdict rules of research round 1, fixed BEFORE the first run. Never edited.

preregistration.question: Does one new, pre-registered entry condition on top of an unchanged Sprint 2c rule give a configuration that passes the Sprint 2c gates on BTC-USDT / ETH-USDT 4H and 6H and is then confirmed by the untouched 12 months — where the Sprint 2c rules themselves passed in only 4 of 108 configurations and the holdout confirmed 1?
preregistration.why: From the failure analyses: Sprint 2 (0 of 42) and 2b (0 of 28) found the edge of long-only timing on BTC/ETH thin and fragile; 2c (4 of 108, 1 confirmed) found the binding gates to be Calmar, Sharpe and the rolling-12-month consistency, that the HMM regime gate cost more return than it saved, and that ETH's rules were weaker than BTC's (no ETH configuration passed); R9 found the mirrored shorts no help; R12 found the families fragile across markets and the S2 breakout's edge not carrying into 2025-26 anywhere. The three conditions below each try to buy consistency by trading less, from the literature of plan section 2.6: cross-market trend (BTC leads the market), attention and volume (Liu & Tsyvinski 2018/2021: attention surges precede gains) and dual momentum (Antonacci: relative strength among trending assets).

H1.title: a BTC-trend condition for ETH entries
H1.rule: ETH-USDT's S1 (time-series momentum) and S2 (Donchian breakout) rules, exactly Sprint 2c's parameters, grids and brackets, with new entries allowed only while BTC-USDT's S1 trend is up — S1 with its Sprint 2 defaults on BTC's candles of the same timeframe (lookbacks 7/14/30 days, at least 2 of 3 positive), aligned bar for bar. Entries only: an open ETH position is left to the base rule's own exits and stop, as the regime gate and the S5 filter do. The condition's parameters are fixed and never in a grid.
H1.comparison: the same S1 / S2 configuration on ETH-USDT without the condition (Sprint 2c's stored numbers, reproduced in this run)
H1.why: no ETH configuration passed in Sprint 2c; BTC's trend is the market's trend, and ETH's rules may be entering against it

H2.title: a volume (attention) confirmation for S1 entries
H2.rule: S1, exactly Sprint 2c's parameters, grid and brackets, on BTC-USDT and ETH-USDT, with new entries allowed only on bars whose volume z-score over the trailing 30 days (the bar's own volume against the trailing mean and standard deviation of the bars of that window) is above 1. Entries only, as above; a run of desired bars that never sees such a bar is skipped. The window and the threshold are fixed and never in a grid.
H2.comparison: the same S1 configuration without the condition (Sprint 2c's stored numbers, reproduced in this run)
H2.why: attention surges precede gains in the crypto literature; S1's losses in 2c came from many small whipsaw entries

H3.title: dual momentum between BTC and ETH
H3.rule: One position in the stronger 90-day performer of BTC-USDT and ETH-USDT, only while BOTH markets' S1 trends are up, as two mutually exclusive legs: DM-BTC on BTC-USDT is long only while BTC's and ETH's S1 trends (the leg's own S1 parameters, from S1's grid, applied to both markets) are up AND BTC's simple return over the lookback is at least ETH's; DM-ETH on ETH-USDT is the mirror with a strict comparison, so an exact tie goes to BTC. Each leg carries S1's ATR stop on its own market and S1's brackets; a leg exits when its condition ends (the position moves to the other leg at the next open) or on its stop. The lookback is fixed and never in a grid.
H3.judged_as: the combined one-position curve per timeframe and regime mode: the legs' stitched out-of-sample bar returns r_b and r_e (identical windows, as the two markets' bar indices are identical) give the combined return (1 + r_b)(1 + r_e) - 1, exact for a fraction-of-equity sizing because at most one leg is in the market at a bar close; the v1c gates on that curve with the profit factor and trade count pooled over the legs' trades and the robustness share taken as the smaller of the legs' shares; the legs are shown as components and are not judged on their own
H3.comparison: S1 on BTC-USDT and S1 on ETH-USDT without the condition (Sprint 2c's stored numbers, reproduced in this run), and the hold + policy controls
H3.why: relative strength among trending assets is the one momentum variant the literature finds robust; it concentrates the one position where the trend is strongest

preregistration.protocol: Sprint 2c's own runner (scripts/run_research_v1c.py loaded as a module, its run_series), with Sprint 2c's defaults: the candidates' grids and brackets (none/tp2/trail1/time30), the S0 filter with the FOMC calendar, the fixed policy sizing vt10/30 crash15/90dh ladder (rebalance 0.25, ladder re-arm 30 days), the regime-v2 entry gate (3-state HMM, bear >= 0.5, fitted on every window's train slice; modes none and gate), the walk-forward (train 540 d, purge 7 d, test 180 d, Sharpe with >= 20 train trades, entries then bracket) and the v1c gates — checked against the stored Sprint 2c run before the study runs; the only change is a feature context that also carries the other market's candles
preregistration.data: the same OKX public 1H and 4H spot candles as Sprint 2c (4H stored, 6H resampled from 1H), frozen at Sprint 2c's data end (bar close <= 2026-10-20T10:00:00+00:00) so the walk-forward and the untouched 12 months (2025-10-20 -> 2026-10-20) are the same calendar window; Binance public funding and open interest for the S0/S5 machinery as in Sprint 2c (the new rules do not use them)
preregistration.reproduction: before any new rule is judged, the same patched code path re-runs hold, S1 and S2 on BTC-USDT and ETH-USDT (4H and 6H, modes none and gate) and must give Sprint 2c's stored walk-forward numbers to 6 decimals, the same trade counts, the same most-selected rules and the same gate verdicts; otherwise the study stops
preregistration.gates: the v1c gates unchanged (research/report_v1c.py GATES): PF > 1.2, max DD < 20 %, Sharpe > 0.7, Calmar > 0.5, >= 75 % of rolling 12-month windows positive, no calendar year below -10 %, >= 30 trades, >= 50 % of +-30 % neighbours profitable
preregistration.verdicts: a configuration passes when it passes every gate on the walk-forward; a hypothesis is 'confirmed' when at least one of its configurations passes and is confirmed by its holdout, 'contradicted by the holdout' when some pass and none is confirmed, and 'failed walk-forward' when none passes; every failing hypothesis gets a failure analysis computed from the numbers beside its base rule
preregistration.holdout: the last 12 months (2025-10-20 -> 2026-10-20), opened once, only for a configuration that passes every walk-forward gate (for H3, the combined curve: then both legs' holdouts are simulated and combined the same way), only by the full pre-registered study (every hypothesis, timeframe and mode, with the reproduction, never --quick); the v1c verdict (positive return, PF > 1, >= 10 trades); every opening goes into an append-only ledger the report shows. CAVEAT, stated before the run: the holdout's falling direction is already known from the R5b and R9 reports (BTC about -26 %, ETH about -39 % over those months, hold + policy negative on every series), and all three conditions reduce time in the market, which flatters them there; a confirmation is therefore necessary but not sufficient, and the paper fleet's forward record is the judge
preregistration.fleet: a confirmed configuration is appended to the paper fleet's shortlist as a new account with a source tag (existing entries and running accounts untouched; a walk-forward pass alone adds nothing); a confirmed H3 adds both legs, which together are the one position; the fleet must be able to load the amended shortlist, otherwise the file is restored and the report says so (the R12 rule)
preregistration.no_changes_after_results: no gate, parameter, condition, market, threshold or verdict rule changes after the results are in; if a gate looks wrong the report says so
